answer: A practical defense is a refundable identity bond: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit that is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. Reputation then accrues only to bonded identities, and peers weight deals by bond age and track record, so a zephyr of cheap throwaway accounts cannot sway a market where lotus-like trusted identities grow slowly, while violet-flagged duplicates forfeit their stake.
